title: Opalcrest - Hosted Vector Relevance Review
summary: Redwood AE/SE walked Opalcrest through hosted embeddings + rerank endpoints. Discussed embedding dims, reranker models, latency/cost tradeoffs, VPC/data retention questions, and pilot next steps. Customer to provide eval dataset; Redwood to send pricing and a runnable rerank notebook.
action_items: Sarah Kim:Send itemized pricing + SKU spreadsheet:2026-11-17
Tom Alvarez:Share sample reranker notebook (notebook + minimal curl examples) and a small benchmark script:2026-11-16
Alex Romero:Provide 500 query sample with relevance labels (CSV or JSONL):2026-11-20
Priya Singh:List top 3 latency SLAs and cost constraints for pilot:2026-11-18
next_steps: Redwood to provision a demo tenant with scoped API keys for Opalcrest
Customer to upload evaluation dataset to shared S3 link
Schedule a 60m pilot kickoff week of 2026-11-22 to run benchmarks
Redwood to send SOC2 summary + network diagram and SSO/SAML doc
transcript:
Meeting header:
Date: 2026-11-13
Start: 16:00 UTC
Duration: ~42 minutes
Attendees: Sarah Kim (Redwood AE), Tom Alvarez (Redwood SE), Jane Liu (Opalcrest PL), Alex Romero (Opalcrest Eng), Priya Singh (Opalcrest DS)

[00:00] Sarah Kim: Hey everyone, thanks for joining, I'm Sarah from Redwood, I'll kick us off. Tom and I will run through a focused hosted-api demo for embeddings and the reranker endpoint tailored to Opalcrest's search stack. Quick check — is the agenda fine?

[00:12] Jane Liu: Yep sounds good. We're mainly trying to understand accuracy lift vs cost and what a short pilot looks like.

[00:20] Tom Alvarez: Cool. Quick context — Redwood hosted API gives you an embeddings endpoint (we support common dims: 768, 1536 depending on model) and an out-of-the-box reranker endpoint that can re-score candidate docs using a smaller cross-encoder style model. Today we'll demo the flow: embed -> ANN retrieval -> rerank via Redwood hosted reranker.

[00:45] Alex Romero: A couple quick things — we currently use Pinecone for vector storage and then a small transformer for re-rank on CPU. We want to see latency numbers and how tight the integration is. Also curious about data retention and VPC peering, our legal team will ask.

[01:05] Sarah Kim: Totally. We'll cover latencies, cost buckets, and security. For retention, hosted defaults to short lived caches but we offer enterprise options in Dedicated/Private for stricter retention and VPC. We'll send the SOC 2 summary and SAML/SSO docs afterwards.

[01:30] Tom Alvarez: Live demo: I'm going to call the embeddings endpoint with a sample query. Note — transcription might call our console 'Redwood Conosle' in some transcriptions — excuse the typos if they show up in the exported notes.

[02:01] [screen share noise] Tom Alvarez: Curl example: curl https://api.redwood.ai/v1/embeddings -d '{"input":"how do I return refunds", "model":"emb-1536-rc" }' — we're getting back a 1536-d vector in about 28-35ms in our hosted region us-west. That of course varies with concurrency and model.

[02:30] Priya Singh: Is 1536 overkill? Our current vector dim is 768 and we see decent results.

[02:40] Tom Alvarez: Good question. 768 vs 1536 tradeoff: higher dims sometimes help nuanced semantic matches but costs per embed are higher and indexing size grows. For many ecommerce / helpdesk datasets 768 is sweet spot. We recommend starting with 768 for pilot unless your eval shows a bump with 1536. We can run both and compare.

[03:10] Sarah Kim: On pricing — embedding calls are metered per request and rerank calls are token-bound; we'll send a two-tab pricing sheet with embedded vs rerank cost estimates for your expected query volume.

[03:36] [background typing] Alex Romero: For rerank — how does the endpoint consume candidates? We want to avoid shipping full docs every time.

[03:45] Tom Alvarez: Reranker endpoint accepts either IDs with a snippet or raw text of top-k candidates. Typical flow: pass query text + top 20 candidate passages (title+snippet) — reranker returns scores. The hosted reranker is optimized to avoid extra KV cache thrash; it uses compact tokenization and can stream top-N results back.

[04:12] Jane Liu: What about latency on rerank for 20 candidates?

[04:18] Tom Alvarez: For a hosted setup we see ~120-220ms depending on model size and sequence length. If you need <100ms consistently we recommend a dedicated pool or smaller reranker variant. There's also batching options — continuous batching can reduce cost but increase median latency slightly.

[04:48] Priya Singh: Do you do quantization for the reranker? We run on CPU in prod and cost is high.

[04:55] Tom Alvarez: Yes — for Dedicated/Private we support int8 quantization and kernel-level optimizations that bring down latency and memory. For hosted we have smaller reranker variants that are efficient; we can also recommend a hybrid: embeddings hosted + rerank on Dedicated if you want predictable latency and lower token costs.

[05:24] Jane Liu: Any gotchas integrating with our Pinecone index?

[05:30] Tom Alvarez: None — you can continue with Pinecone. Just export vectors and use Redwood embeddings to compare. For a simpler pilot we ingest vectors into Pinecone and call Redwood reranker over top-k hits. If you want tighter coupling, Redwood can host vector storage in Dedicated and avoid extra egress.

[06:02] Alex Romero: On security lines — can we do VPC peering or private link to avoid public egress? And KMS?

[06:12] Sarah Kim: Yes, for Private/Dedicated we provide VPC peering, private link options, and customer-managed KMS/HSM integrations. For hosted customers we offer encryption at rest and in transit and can sign BAAs and provide SOC2 docs. We'll attach network diagram and SSO/SAML guide.

[06:40] Priya Singh: What's the default logging/PII retention window? Our compliance requires 30 day auto-delete for raw request payloads.

[06:50] Tom Alvarez: Hosted defaults to 90 days for audit logs but request payload retention is configurable on enterprise plans; we can set shorter retention in Dedicated/Private. We'll include that in the security doc.

[07:08] Sarah Kim: Quick live example of a rerank call. I'm going to pass the query and top 10 candidate snippets — you'll see the score output.

[07:25] [curl noise] Tom Alvarez: Sample payload: {"query":"refund policy when item damaged","candidates":[{"id":"c1","text":"policy: refunds for damaged items within 30 days..."}, ...]} We get back a JSON array with scores and a recommended top-3. Latency here was ~150ms.

[08:10] Jane Liu: That seems reasonable. Can you show how to tune thresholding for precision vs recall?

[08:18] Tom Alvarez: Sure — typical approach: use rerank score threshold + topN cutoff. We also provide monotonic calibration and a confidence score. In Console (Redwood Consoel in some notes) you can set thresholds and preview changes on a small sample.

[09:00] Sarah Kim: I'm going to switch to the Console to show the evaluation tab — we have a built in eval runner that lets you run a labeled set and compare precision@k and MRR across model variants and embeddings dims.

[09:20] [screen share] Tom Alvarez: Here you can upload a CSV of query+gold doc ids, select candidate retrieval pipeline (your Pinecone top20) and reranker model, and we'll run batch scoring. It's a good way to get lift numbers quickly.

[09:44] Priya Singh: How much data do you need for a meaningful test?

[09:50] Tom Alvarez: For initial signal 300-500 queries with relevance labels is useful; for stable results we like 2k+. For pilot, 500 is a good starting point.

[10:05] Alex Romero: We can pull 500 queries. We'll also include some long-tail queries.

[10:10] Sarah Kim: Great. We'll also show how Optimize suggests batching and quantization settings to balance cost. The Optimize module will highlight weird token length distributions and recommend model/quantization.

[10:30] Jane Liu: What's the expected cost delta between doing rerank on CPU vs Redwood hosted reranker?

[10:40] Tom Alvarez: Hard to say without volumes — rough thumb: if you're running rerank on large CPU fleets, hosted reranker is often cheaper at scale because of GPU efficiency and deduped compute. We'll provide cost estimates in the pricing sheet.

[11:05] [brief pause]

[11:20] Tom Alvarez: A few implementation notes: keep candidate passages concise to reduce token count; use batch rerank for heavy traffic; consider prefix/KV caching for repeated queries to drop per-token cost. Also watch for sequence length — long documents increase rerank time.

[11:55] Priya Singh: Does Redwood support function/tool calling or structured output in rerank — like returning metadata tags?

[12:05] Tom Alvarez: Reranker returns scores and optionally structured payloads we can surface; we also support a small set of function-style outputs. For heavy structured extraction we recommend a downstream specialized call.

[12:30] Jane Liu: Who would be our contact for the pilot?

[12:34] Sarah Kim: I'll be the AE and Tom the SE; Tom will run the technical onboarding. For contracts you can loop in procurement, but pilot is usually a short free eval.

[12:50] Alex Romero: Any known limits on concurrent requests for hosted? We expect spikes during peak hours.

[12:58] Tom Alvarez: Hosted has soft rate limits per account; for spikes we can enable rate-limit increases or recommend Dedicated capacity with reserved throughput. Also smart routing can fallback to smaller model variants if we hit capacity.

[13:22] Jane Liu: We occasionally have strict residency needs — Europe-only datasets. Does Redwood support region pinning?

[13:30] Sarah Kim: Yes, you can pin workloads to regions and we have EU regions. For strict data residency and compliance we recommend Private or Dedicated in a selected region.

[14:00] Priya Singh: Can you show a short walkthrough of the sample rerank notebook?

[14:06] Tom Alvarez: Sure — opening notebook. The notebook shows: fetch top-k from Pinecone, call Redwood rerank endpoint with candidates, compute precision@5. There's a minimal benchmark cell that runs 100 queries and reports avg latency and p95. We'll attach this notebook.

[14:40] [typing, minor audio glitch] Tom Alvarez: Run benchmark: avg embed latency 32ms, avg ANN retrieval ~12ms (depends on Pinecone), rerank avg 160ms; end-to-end topK re-score ~210ms per query in these test conditions.

[15:05] Jane Liu: Ok — that aligns with our needs for now. We might want to move rerank to Dedicated later if latency needs tighten.

[15:18] Sarah Kim: Totally reasonable. We'll show cost projections for both paths.

[15:30] Alex Romero: A question on SLA — for Dedicated what are uptime/latency SLAs?

[15:38] Sarah Kim: Dedicated comes with a 99.9% uptime SLA and latency targets per model size; we'll include exact SLA language in the contract template.

[15:50] Priya Singh: Any compliance packages for healthcare datasets?

[15:54] Sarah Kim: We have compliance add-ons, and Private deployments for HIPAA-level requirements; we also support BAA execution. We'll pass the relevant packet.

[16:12] [wrap-up tone] Sarah Kim: To recap: Redwood will send pricing, SOC2 + network diagram, sample rerank notebook, and provision a demo tenant. Opalcrest will share 500 queries with labels and list SLA/cost constraints. We'll reconvene for a pilot kickoff week of 2026-11-22.

[16:40] Jane Liu: That sounds good, thanks.

[16:45] Alex Romero: Thanks folks.

[16:48] Priya Singh: Thanks, bye.

[16:50] Sarah Kim: Thanks everyone, end call.

End transcript.
